Research for **Pick Your AI**, a PCPartPicker-inspired AI system builder. Repository: https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research

**Structure:** seven workstream parents (T0–T6) with native sub-issues for each component. T3 Knowledge & Retrieval, T4 Agents & Integrations, and T5 Training & Fine-Tuning are optional capabilities.

**Fields**
- **Status:** Backlog · Ready · In Progress · In Review (draft decision record open) · Blocked · Done (merged and acceptance criteria met). Set from evidence only.
- **Priority:** research sequencing, not product importance. Critical is the foundation core path; High is core and consumes Critical outputs; Medium is optional capabilities and operational depth; Low is nice-to-have.
- **Tier:** T0–T6 (option labels include the tier name).
- **Readiness:** Ready · Needs input · Blocked · Awaiting decision.
- **Ownership:** GitHub Assignees (source of truth).
- **Work Type:** Epic · Research · Specification · Dataset · Validation.
- **Research Confidence:** Unverified · Low · Medium · High.
- **Dependency Status:** Unblocked · Waiting · Blocked (mirrors native "blocked by" relationships; Readiness records broader readiness).

**Views:** Workstream overview (hierarchy) · Research backlog by priority · Ready to research · Blocked or awaiting decision · Unassigned or missing metadata.

**Dependencies:** native "blocked by" is used only for genuine prerequisites (currently #42 ← #40). Information and compatibility relationships are listed in each issue body and may be cyclic, e.g. model ↔ GPU ↔ inference engine.

Conventions: https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md · Dependency map: https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/DEPENDENCIES.md

content.body:
## Product question
What is the user building, under which constraints and deployment mode, and how does the builder represent, validate, price-source, save, and share the resulting configuration?

## Scope
Entry point of every build plus the cross-cutting builder model (component schema, compatibility rules, catalog data sourcing, saved builds). Every other workstream consumes T0 outputs.

## Research sub-issues
Tracked as native sub-issues. Progress appears in the sub-issue panel and in the [Project](https://github.com/orgs/Pick-Your-AI/projects/1).
- #2
- #3
- #40
- #41
- #42

## Handoffs and boundaries
- T0 owns the shared component schema and rule format (#40); component issues supply category attributes and rules in that format.
- T0 owns catalog data-source policy (#41): where builder facts and prices come from, reuse terms, freshness, and evidence grading. User knowledge sources belong to T3 (#13).
- Pricing *units and aggregation* belong to T6 Cost Estimate (#39); raw price provenance rules belong to #41.

## Workstream done when (research completion)
- [x] All sub-issues are closed with merged decision records that meet their acceptance criteria
- [x] The handoffs above are confirmed by the affected workstream owners
- [x] A workstream summary at `research/T0-configuration/README.md` lists decisions, rules contributed to #40, and open questions

This tracks research only. Implementation is out of scope for this repository.

## Owner
Owner: GitHub assignee (source of truth).

See the [research method](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/RESEARCH_METHOD.md), [dependency map](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/DEPENDENCIES.md), and [contributing guide](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

<!-- research-contract-v1 -->
## Contract and submission format

- [Canonical schemas and component registry](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/tree/a222013c1f0106159132564d05e5d24666ad6342/contracts/v1/schemas): use these exact kinds, field names, types, and required values.

[PR #44](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/pull/44) was merged on 2026-10-16. These links retain the imported revision; current canonical schemas and workflow are on [`main`](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/tree/main/contracts/v1).

- [Research workflow](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/a222013c1f0106159132564d05e5d24666ad6342/docs/RESEARCH_WORKFLOW.md) and [all-kind mapping](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/a222013c1f0106159132564d05e5d24666ad6342/docs/CONTRACT_MAPPING.md).
- [Research note template](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/a222013c1f0106159132564d05e5d24666ad6342/templates/research-note.md). Keep the existing decision-record path and acceptance criteria.
- Component sub-issues retain their owners. Confirm cross-workstream field and rule handoffs during review; importing the contract does not complete the research.
- Include validation results and unresolved evidence/compatibility questions in the research PR. The included example data is synthetic, never a vendor source.

<!-- maintainer-research-prompts-start -->
## Maintainer execution prompt

- [Runbook and checkout guidance](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/69cdd7d7f96a0b7f25c997ab6970109a7d144eec/prompts/README.md)

- [Prompt publication / review PR #74](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/pull/74) — merged to `main` as [`708bd94`](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/commit/708bd94fa49482235308fd79fcc5f8669a29ce3d). The pinned prompt below is historical publication guidance; use current repository instructions and live issue state. Guidance merge is not research acceptance.
- [Canonical T0 parent issue](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/issues/1) · [Research Project](https://github.com/orgs/Pick-Your-AI/projects/1)

Use a repository checkout containing revision `69cdd7d7f96a` (branch `docs/maintainer-research-prompts`). For an existing clone, fetch that branch and use a separate worktree; preserve any active work. Paste this into your coding/research agent from that checkout:

```text
Read AGENTS.md and the current contributor/research workflow instructions.
Then read prompts/SHARED.md and prompts/T0.md.
Execute the T0 research workstream within my existing authority.
Refresh live issues, Project fields, assignees, and active runs first.
Coordinate with the existing owner/run; preserve acceptance criteria and the
frozen v1 contract. Obtain required reviews before merge or closure.
Complete independent work and report exact remaining blockers.
```

Publishing this handoff does not start a run, change assignments or Project status, or satisfy acceptance criteria. The v1 contract was adopted in PR #44; older references to it being under review are historical. Use live Project field IDs/options as explained in the shared rules.


Organization/public metadata maintenance is a separate assignment: hand off evidence of outdated public claims to [organization maintenance issue #2](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/.github/issues/2) using the [maintenance prompt](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/69cdd7d7f96a0b7f25c997ab6970109a7d144eec/prompts/ORGANIZATION.md). This informational handoff adds no research deliverable or blocker and does not start a maintenance run.

content.body:
> Workstream: #1 (T0 Configuration) · Owner: GitHub assignee. Priority and readiness are tracked in the [Project](https://github.com/orgs/Pick-Your-AI/projects/1).

## User decision
What is the user trying to build, and which goals and constraints should filter and rank every later choice?

## Scope
**In scope**
- Workload taxonomy (e.g. conversational, extraction, generation, coding, multimodal, batch)
- Input/output modalities
- Quality, latency, and throughput targets expressed as ranges
- Traffic, concurrency, and volume assumptions
- Data sensitivity and residency constraints
- Budget ceiling and currency
- Capability needs that activate optional workstreams (retrieval → T3, tools/agents → T4, customisation → T5)

**Out of scope (owned elsewhere)**
- Model capability claims (#6) and benchmark methods (#36)
- Cost calculation (#39)
- Deployment-mode tradeoffs (#3)

## Research questions
- What is the smallest question set that meaningfully filters downstream options?
- How should targets be expressed when the user does not know them (defaults, ranges, `unknown`)?
- Which inputs activate or remove T3, T4, and T5?
- How do workload requirements become evaluation criteria in #36?
- Should a build support more than one workload?

## Deliverable
A decision record at `research/T0-configuration/workload-use-case.md` using the [research method](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/RESEARCH_METHOD.md) template, merged by a pull request that references this issue. Use a checklist in this issue for small steps; open a sub-issue only for separately owned work.

## Comparison fields and evidence
Minimum fields (refine as evidence requires):
- `workload_type`
- `modalities_in / modalities_out`
- `latency target (percentile, unit)`
- `throughput / concurrency`
- `volume (requests and tokens per period)`
- `data classification`
- `residency constraint`
- `budget (amount, currency, period)`
- `capability flags`

Evidence: primary sources only (publisher documentation, pricing pages, model cards, licenses, specifications, benchmark publications), each with URL, access date, version, and region/currency for prices. Label every number as measured, published, or estimated and record its conditions. Grade evidence using the policy from #41.

## Dependencies and relationships
| Relationship | Issues |
| --- | --- |
| Information inputs (uses facts from; not a blocker) | — |
| Compatibility relationships (bidirectional; may be cyclic) | — |
| Blocked by (native GitHub dependency) | — |
| Downstream consumers | #3, #6, #7, #10, #36, #39, #40 |

Information inputs and compatibility relationships do not set execution order. Start with what is available, record assumptions, and revisit. See the [dependency map](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/DEPENDENCIES.md).

## Acceptance criteria (research completion)
- [x] Taxonomy with definitions and boundary examples
- [x] Mapping table: each input → downstream filters, rules, or evaluation criteria it drives
- [x] Each input has a type, unit, allowed range, and `unknown` handling
- [x] Activation rules for T3/T4/T5
- [x] Decision record merged at `research/T0-configuration/workload-use-case.md` following the research method
- [x] Candidate set covers the relevant deployment modes (API / managed / self-hosted) or states why a mode does not apply
- [x] Comparison fields defined with type, unit, and evidence requirement
- [x] Compatibility rules and warnings use the shared format from #40; verified rules are separated from hypotheses
- [x] Every factual or numeric claim cites a primary source with access date (and version / region / currency where relevant)
- [x] Each handoff listed under Dependencies is confirmed by the consuming issue's owner (link the comment or PR review)
- [x] Open questions recorded with a named follow-up owner

Closing this issue means the research deliverable is complete and reviewed. It does **not** mean the builder implements it.

## Open questions
- Single vs multi-workload builds

> Workstream: #8 (T2 Infrastructure) · Owner: GitHub assignee. Priority and readiness are tracked in the [Project](https://github.com/orgs/Pick-Your-AI/projects/1).

## User decision
Which accelerator, and how many, are needed to serve the selected model at the target load?

## Scope
**In scope**
- Accelerator catalog
- Memory estimation: weights × precision + KV cache + runtime overhead
- Throughput and latency estimation approach, concurrency, headroom
- Multi-GPU / parallelism requirements
- Effect of fine-tuned adapters (input from #33)
- Clear separation of measured vs estimated values

**Out of scope (owned elsewhere)**
- Training compute estimates (#31 reuses this catalog)
- Hosting prices (#9)

## Research questions
- Which estimation method is defensible, and with what error range?
- Which published measurements exist, and under what conditions?
- How are multi-GPU requirements represented?
- Is CPU or edge inference in scope?

## Deliverable
A decision record at `research/T2-infrastructure/gpu-compute.md` using the [research method](https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/RESEARCH_METHOD.md) template, merged by a pull request that references this issue. Use a checklist in this issue for small steps; open a sub-issue only for separately owned work.

## Comparison fields and evidence
Minimum fields (refine as evidence requires):
- `accelerator id`
- `vendor`
- `memory capacity`
- `memory bandwidth`
- `supported precisions`
- `interconnect`
- `sizing output: memory range, GPU count`
- `assumptions (precision, batch, context, concurrency)`
- `measured vs estimated flag`
- `source`

Evidence: primary sources only (publisher documentation, pricing pages, model cards, licenses, specifications, benchmark publications), each with URL, access date, version, and region/currency for prices. Label every number as measured, published, or estimated and record its conditions. Grade evidence using the policy from #41.
